references.text: The context of the parable: a man of noble birth went to a distant country to receive kingly power. In [ref:Luk 19:12|Luke 19:12], we find the background for his return in verse 15, where he has received the kingdom and now demands an account.

In the parable of the talents in [ref:Matt 25:19|Matthew 25:19], the master returns after a long time and settles accounts with his servants—a clear parallel to the lord in Luke 19:15 calling his servants to him to hear what they have gained.

In [ref:Matt 25:14-15|Matthew 25:14-15], a master entrusts his servants with different sums of money before he goes away, paralleling the lord in the parable of Luke who gave his servants ten minas and now, upon his return, wants to know what they have achieved.

[ref:Rom 14:10-12|Romans 14:10-12] speaks of us all standing before God's judgment seat and giving an account. This corresponds to the theme in Luke 19:15, where the servants must give an account of their stewardship to the master.

[ref:2 Kor 5:10|2 Corinthians 5:10] says that we all must appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive what is due for what we have done in the body. This idea of giving an account corresponds to the lord in Luke 19:15 wanting to know what the servants have gained from the money.

In [ref:Luk 16:2|Luke 16:2], the master demands an account from his steward: "Give an account of your stewardship." This is a closely parallel motif to Luke 19:15, where the lord calls the servants in to hear about their management of the minas.
[ref:1 Pet 4:5|1 Peter 4:5] reminds us that all must give an account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead. The theme of giving an account before the Lord connects with Luke 19:15.

In [ref:Åp 11:15|Revelation 11:15], it is proclaimed that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and his Anointed, and he shall reign forever and ever. This corresponds to the man in the parable returning after receiving kingly power ([ref:Luk 19:15|Luke 19:15]).

In [ref:Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14], the Son of Man receives dominion and kingly power from the Ancient of Days. This prophecy forms the background for the parable's image of one who goes away to receive kingly power and then returns, as we see in Luke 19:15.
